planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis or fence in full sun to partial shade; Celestial is deer-resistant like most honeysuckle vines in this breeding line.

directions: Plant against a trellis, fence, or arbor in full sun to partial shade; Celestial is a named Lonicera vine selection valued for its twining habit and wide hardiness range across zones 4-11. Give it a sturdy support to climb and keep the root zone mulched and cool, a condition most honeysuckle vines favor even when the top growth reaches into brighter light. Like most honeysuckle vines in cultivation it is deer-resistant, a practical advantage for a vine grown where deer pressure is a concern.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis or fence in full sun to partial shade; Peaches and Cream climbs by twining and needs a support to train upward.

directions: Plant against a trellis, fence, or arbor in full sun to partial shade; Peaches and Cream is a named Lonicera vine selection suited to the wide zone 4-11 hardiness range typical of this group of honeysuckle hybrids. Provide a sturdy support for the twining stems and mulch the root zone to keep it cool and moist, even as the vine climbs into brighter light above. Like most honeysuckle vines it is generally deer-resistant, making it a reliable choice for a garden with deer pressure.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis or fence in full sun to partial shade; this Chinese species is a true-species relative of the hybrid 'Goldflame', not the same plant.

directions: Plant against a trellis, fence, or arbor in full sun to partial shade; Lonicera tragophylla is a true Chinese species honeysuckle, distinct from the popular 'Goldflame' hybrid already in cultivation, bearing bright yellow tubular flowers on a vigorous twining vine. It tolerates a broad hardiness range from zone 4 through zone 11 and benefits from a sturdy support and a cool, mulched root zone even as it climbs into sun. Like most honeysuckle vines it is generally resistant to deer browsing.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis or fence in full sun to partial shade; this Chinese species honeysuckle tolerates the same broad zone 4-11 range as its genus relatives.

directions: Plant against a trellis, fence, or arbor in full sun to partial shade; Lonicera giraldii is a Chinese species honeysuckle climbing vine, a less commonly grown relative of the better-known garden honeysuckles. Give it a sturdy support and a cool, mulched root zone to establish, and expect it to tolerate a broad hardiness range similar to other species in this genus. It is generally resistant to deer browsing, consistent with most Lonicera vines in cultivation.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis or through a shrub in full sun to partial shade; Little Butterfly is in Pruning Group 3, cut back hard to about a foot in late winter.

directions: Plant against a trellis or let it scramble through a supporting shrub in full sun to partial shade; Little Butterfly is a Clematis viticella selection, joining dozens of other named viticella cultivars in the nodding-flower, summer-blooming group known for vigor and resistance to clematis wilt. It falls in Pruning Group 3, meaning the entire vine is cut back hard to about a foot above ground in late winter each year, which keeps growth renewed and flowering strong. It is generally deer-resistant and hardy through zone 4-8.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis in full sun to partial shade; Ruby Wedding is in Pruning Group 3, cut back hard in late winter like other texensis clematis.

directions: Plant against a trellis or fence in full sun to partial shade; Ruby Wedding is a Clematis texensis selection, part of the Texas-native scarlet clematis lineage prized for its tulip-shaped, nodding flowers and heat tolerance compared to many other clematis groups. It falls in Pruning Group 3, cut back hard in late winter to encourage strong new flowering growth. It tolerates a wide hardiness range from zone 4 through zone 11 and is generally resistant to deer browsing.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis in full sun to partial shade; Radiance is in Pruning Group 3, cut back hard in late winter like other texensis clematis.

directions: Plant against a trellis or fence in full sun to partial shade; Radiance is a Clematis texensis selection from the Texas-native scarlet clematis lineage, grown for its tulip-shaped nodding flowers and better heat tolerance than many large-flowered hybrid clematis groups. It falls in Pruning Group 3, cut back hard to encourage vigorous new flowering growth each spring. It tolerates a wide hardiness range from zone 4 through zone 11 and is generally resistant to deer browsing.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis in full sun to partial shade; Maxima is in Pruning Group 3, cut back hard in late winter like other texensis clematis.

directions: Plant against a trellis or fence in full sun to partial shade; Maxima is a Clematis texensis selection bred for larger flowers than the typical narrow tulip-shaped blooms of this Texas-native scarlet clematis lineage. It falls in Pruning Group 3, cut back hard in late winter to renew flowering growth, and tolerates a wide hardiness range from zone 4 through zone 11. Like other texensis cultivars it is generally resistant to deer browsing and tolerates more summer heat than many large-flowered hybrid clematis groups.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a sturdy structure in full sun; Jersey Peach is a vigorous self-clinging vine that needs a strong support able to bear its weight at maturity.

directions: Plant against a strong pergola, arbor, or wall in full sun; Jersey Peach is a named trumpet vine selection joining a wide range of other Campsis cultivars in cultivation, grown for its peach-toned trumpet flowers through summer that draw hummingbirds reliably. Like other trumpet vines it is extremely vigorous and self-clinging, so site it only where a structure can bear substantial weight and where its aggressive spread by root suckers can be managed. Prune hard each year to keep growth in bounds, since left unchecked it can quickly overwhelm a smaller support.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a wall or trellis in part shade to shade; Ercilla self-clings by aerial roots similar to ivy, suiting a shaded north-facing wall.

directions: Plant against a wall or trellis in part shade to shade; Ercilla is a South American evergreen climbing vine in the Phytolaccaceae, self-clinging by aerial roots in a manner similar to ivy, making it well suited to a shaded, sheltered wall where few flowering vines perform well. It carries small, inconspicuous flowers, grown chiefly for its glossy evergreen foliage and climbing habit rather than floral display. Give it a sheltered site out of harsh winter wind at the colder end of its hardiness range, and water regularly through the first season to establish.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis in full sun to partial shade; Damsel's Delight is a named passionflower hybrid hardy through zone 6-11.

directions: Plant against a trellis or fence in full sun to partial shade; Damsel's Delight is a named passionflower hybrid grown for its intricate, uniquely structured flowers typical of the genus, hardy through a broad zone 6-11 range. Provide a sturdy support for the fast-growing twining tendrils, and cut the vine back hard in late winter in colder parts of its range, since it typically dies back to the root and resprouts vigorously each spring. Some Passiflora cultivars produce edible passion fruit, though flowering ornament is the primary draw for named hybrids like this one.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis or let it scramble over a shrub in full sun to partial shade; Sapelo is a selection of the small-flowered native yellow passionflower.

directions: Plant against a trellis or let it scramble over a shrub in full sun to partial shade; Sapelo is a named selection of Passiflora lutea, the small-flowered native yellow passionflower of the eastern and southern United States, distinct from the much showier tropical hybrid passionflowers. Its diminutive greenish-yellow flowers are easily overlooked but it serves as a host plant for gulf fritillary and other butterfly larvae, making it a worthwhile addition to a native pollinator garden. It is more cold-hardy than the showier Passiflora hybrids, tolerating zone 6 winters with root hardiness.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring against a trellis or let it spread by suckers in full sun to partial shade; Alba Supernova is a white-flowered selection of the native maypop passionflower.

directions: Plant against a trellis in full sun to partial shade; Alba Supernova is a distinct white-flowered selection of maypop, the cold-hardy native passionflower, differing from the plain white 'Alba' form already grown in cultivation. It produces the species' intricate, fringed flowers followed by the edible, egg-shaped maypop fruit in late summer and fall. Being root-hardy well into zone 6, it typically dies back to the ground each winter and resprouts vigorously, spreading by root suckers that may need containment in a smaller garden.
